status: Exploratory retrospective specification, written before inspecting this expanded analysis; earlier huck results were already known.
question: How do receiving teams change their play on their second and later possessions within the same point?
scope: 2026 final regular-season games in the preserved ShownSpace export and audited public UFA events. Team began point receiving, whether it eventually holds or is broken.
comparisons: First vs second vs third-or-later team possession
Within-team opening vs all subsequent possessions
main_filter: Exclude possessions containing recorded team timeout events 3 or 5. Preserve their original possession numbers. Keep injury and penalty events as flags; exclude entire points with timeouts or injuries only in sensitivity analyses.
physical_throws: Retain every actual attempted throw including centering, drops and throwaways. Stalls and Callahan catches can end a zero-throw possession.
metrics: Mean and median throws, separately in possessions ending in goals and turnovers
Goals divided by resolved goal-or-turnover possessions; period-ending possessions listed separately
Possessions containing any huck and containing a huck within their first three throws
Huck choice at throw 1, throws 2–3, throws 4–6, and throws 7+
Actual huck catches per attempt, drops separately, and recorded expected completion
Scoring after a completed huck as a descriptive continuation result
Association of prior point activity with early hucking on subsequent possessions
huck_definition: Straight-line distance >40 yards and forward gain >30 yards. Repeat principal comparisons using >40 forward yards.
huck_possession_eligibility: For the main huck comparisons retain starts at least 40 yards from the attacking goal line: first recorded throwing Y <=60 on the 120-yard coordinate system. This is a transparent working definition of sufficient room to huck, not a discovered optimum. Repeat with Y <=50 and Y <=70, and unrestricted as sensitivity checks. Do not apply this exclusion to scoring or possession throw counts.
starting_location: First recorded throwing or stall location; actual location where possession was won is not observed for every gain. Coordinate adjustments must describe this proxy accurately.
adjustment: Descriptive regression standardization using starting longitudinal and lateral position, team, opponent, quarter and raw point-start period time where available. Additional within-game and common-field-region sensitivity checks. No chosen-throw endpoint, future outcome, or eventual hold as a pre-choice control.
uncertainty: Whole-game bootstrap for observed estimates and differences. Regression covariance clustered by game. Team comparisons have only 11–12 games; use team game-count t references and Holm correction both within each 22-team metric family and across all 132 team contrasts. This is a pragmatic small-sample precaution, not exact finite-sample inference. Apply Holm to 16 principal league contrasts and six team-heterogeneity tests. Report effects and uncertainty; no p-value-driven selection of outcomes or teams.
amendment_2026_11_05: After inspecting initial results, added throws-2–3 and exact-third-possession checks; separately report second-to-third-or-later contrasts as exploratory. Changed actual-catch adjustment from fixed logit(CP) offset to a fitted logit(CP) covariate because production training target/calibration to actual catches is unverified. Preserve the original offset model as sensitivity. Added correction across all 132 team contrasts so searching six metrics does not overstate team evidence.
selection: All opening possessions define the baseline. A matched subset of points that reach a regain is outcome-selected and cannot define a scoring baseline. Later throw stages include only surviving possessions.
interpretation: Fewer throws describes fewer passing actions. Early hucking can fit the impatience hypothesis but cannot demonstrate fatigue, intent or that hucking causes better scoring. Receiving-team role is not proof of unchanged personnel.
